title: Teachers’ perceptions of generative ai integration: A qualitative case study at a university in Baluchistan
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines university educators’ perceptions of integrating generative artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education, with a focus on how such tools affect teaching practices in a resource-constrained context. The authors frame the study using the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework to understand how technology, pedagogy, and content knowledge interact when educators adopt generative AI for instructional work.

The study is a qualitative case study conducted at a university in Baluchistan, Pakistan, with 25 faculty members from multiple departments. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions, then analyzed thematically. Participants discussed generative AI as a tool that can streamline lesson planning, improve access to resources, support differentiated and personalized instruction, and provide data-driven insights into student engagement and performance.

At the same time, educators expressed concerns about academic integrity, data privacy, unequal access to devices and internet, and insufficient institutional support. Many participants also emphasized the need for sustained professional development, mentorship, and clear policy guidance to use AI effectively and ethically. The paper concludes that generative AI has strong potential to improve teaching in higher education, but successful adoption depends on robust training, supportive infrastructure, and explicit ethical and institutional frameworks.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI tools that can create content, support instructional tasks, personalize learning, and provide feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: A qualitative case study examined university educators’ perceptions of generative AI integration in higher education, with emphasis on lesson planning, personalized instruction, resource access, and engagement; no specific product was named.

findings.finding_summary: Educators generally viewed generative AI positively for streamlining lesson planning, improving resource accessibility, and saving time. The paper reports that 80% of participants (20/25) highlighted these benefits, but no effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Participant perceptions of lesson planning efficiency and resource accessibility

findings.finding_summary: Participants reported that generative AI supported personalized instruction and differentiation, with 68% of educators noting improved ability to tailor materials to diverse student needs. The study is qualitative and reports participant perceptions rather than a quantitative effect size.
findings.measure: Perceived ability to differentiate instruction and personalize materials

findings.finding_summary: Educators stated that generative AI helped provide real-time feedback and analyze student performance data, supporting earlier intervention and student monitoring. The paper reports these as perceived benefits from interviews and focus groups, with no effect size provided.
findings.measure: Perceived real-time feedback and student performance analytics

findings.finding_summary: The study found strong demand for professional development: 70% of participants emphasized ongoing training needs, and 65% wanted mentorship or communities of practice. This indicates that effective adoption depended on institutional support and teacher capacity building rather than tool performance metrics.
findings.measure: Perceived professional development needs for AI integration

findings.finding_summary: Educators expressed concerns about academic integrity, data privacy, limited institutional support, and unequal student access to technology. Approximately 60% raised ethical concerns and 40% raised access concerns, indicating barriers to implementation in this context.
findings.measure: Perceived ethical, privacy, support, and access barriers to AI integration

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study using interviews and focus groups, which provides contextual insight but not causal evidence. The methodology is appropriate for perceptions research, but it does not support strong effect estimation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports broadly positive perceived benefits for instructional planning, personalization, and feedback, but these are self-reported and not quantified with effect sizes. The practical impact appears promising yet unclear because implementation barriers and institutional constraints are substantial.
